# 07 — i18n (Internationalization)

> Challenge: #8

## Problem
All micro-frontends render one page, so they must show one language and switch it together. i18next keeps the language
and every loaded translation in one instance; if each app initializes the shared instance itself, the last `init`
resets everyone. Translations belong to the team that writes the UI and ship with its deploy, so the shell cannot
bundle them — and when a remote loads them by URL, a relative URL resolves against the **host's** origin, not the
remote's.

## Solution
- **`i18next` + `react-i18next` are MF singletons** in all four `webpack.config.js` (same options as react-query).
- **`@mf/i18n`** (`packages/i18n`, stateless, bundled into each app):
  - `createI18n(language)` — `i18next.createInstance().use(createNamespaceLoaderBackend()).use(initReactI18next)
    .init({ lng, fallbackLng: false, supportedLngs: ['en', 'uk'], ns: [], defaultNS: false, … })`.
  - `createNamespaceLoaderBackend()` — an i18next backend with `registerNamespace(ns, loader)`; `read(lng, ns)` calls
    the registered loader.
  - `useNamespaceTranslation(ns, loader)` — registers the loader on the instance from context, returns
    `useTranslation(ns).t`.
- **Shell owns the instance and the language.** `bootstrap.tsx`:
  ```tsx
  const i18n = createI18n(readStoredLanguage()); // shell:language, narrowed on read
  <I18nextProvider i18n={i18n}> … <Suspense fallback={null}><App /></Suspense>
  ```
  `i18n/LanguageSwitcher.tsx` (`<select>` in the header) calls `i18n.changeLanguage(next)`; `use-language.ts` persists
  `shell:language` and sets `<html lang>`. The shell translates its own texts, including the `label` it passes to
  `cart/CartWidget` (the prop contract did not change).
- **Each app owns one namespace** named after its container and keeps `src/i18n/locales/{en,uk}.json`:
  ```ts
  // apps/catalog/src/i18n/use-catalog-translation.ts
  const loadCatalogBundle: Record<Language, () => Promise<{ default: object }>> = {
    en: () => import(/* webpackChunkName: "locale-en" */ './locales/en.json'),
    uk: () => import(/* webpackChunkName: "locale-uk" */ './locales/uk.json'),
  };
  export function useCatalogTranslation() {
    return useNamespaceTranslation('catalog', (language) => loadCatalogBundle[language]());
  }
  ```
  `Record<Language, …>` makes a new language a type error until every app adds its file.
- **Standalone remotes** create their own instance in `bootstrap.tsx` (`createI18n(DEFAULT_LANGUAGE)`); `exposed/` never
  does.
- **Formatting through `Intl`** via i18next's built-in formatters: `"price": "{{value, currency(USD)}}"` →
  `$89.00` / `89,00 USD`; `"placedAt": "{{value, datetime}}"` with `formatParams: { value: { dateStyle: 'medium',
  timeStyle: 'short' } }` → `Oct 1, 2026, 1:00 PM` / `1 жовт. 2026 р., 13:00`. Plurals go through `Intl.PluralRules`:
  Ukrainian needs `_one/_few/_many/_other` (`21 штука`, `22 штуки`, `15 штук`), English only `_one/_other`.
- Product names and descriptions come from the API and stay untranslated (server content).

## How it works
- **Who calls `init`.** Only code that runs in `bootstrap.tsx`: the shell's always, a remote's only standalone — when
  hosted, the shell loads the remote's `remoteEntry.js` and its exposes, never its `bootstrap.tsx`. Verified:
  `createI18n(` appears only in the four `bootstrap.tsx` files, and `__mfDebug()` shows one `i18next` 26.4.7 and one
  `react-i18next` 17.0.20, both provided by `shell` and loaded.
- **How the remote's text reaches the shell's instance.** `<I18nextProvider>` is a context of the shared
  `react-i18next`, so `useContext(I18nContext)` inside catalog returns the shell's instance. `useNamespaceTranslation`
  registers catalog's loader on that instance's backend (`instance.modules.backend.registerNamespace`), then
  `useTranslation('catalog')` sees the namespace is not loaded, calls `i18n.loadNamespaces('catalog')` and suspends.
  i18next calls `backend.read('en', 'catalog')` → the loader → `import('./locales/en.json')`.
- **Why it comes from :3001.** That `import()` is compiled into catalog's bundle as a chunk load through catalog's own
  webpack runtime: `__webpack_require__.p + 'locale-en.js'`. `publicPath: 'auto'` set `__webpack_require__.p` from the
  URL of the script that started the runtime — `http://localhost:3001/remoteEntry.js` — so the request goes to
  `http://localhost:3001/locale-en.js`. Each container has its own runtime, chunk registry (`webpackChunkcatalog`,
  from `uniqueName`) and public path, which is why three `locale-en.js` files on three origins do not clash.
- **Lazy, one request per app per language.** Measured in the browser (fresh load of `/catalog`, `en`):
  `:3000/locale-en.js`, `:3001/locale-en.js`; opening the mini-cart adds `:3002/locale-en.js`; switching to `uk` adds
  exactly `:3000`, `:3001`, `:3002` `locale-uk.js`; switching back to `en` adds nothing; opening Account adds
  `:3003/locale-en.js` only. Same result on the production build (served statically).
- **Atomic switch.** `changeLanguage('uk')` → i18next's `loadResources` asks the backend for `uk` of every namespace in
  `options.ns` (each `loadNamespaces` call appended to it) and emits `languageChanged` only after all of them arrive.
  react-i18next re-renders every app in one pass with the bundles already in the store — no Suspense fallback. Checked
  with a `MutationObserver` on `<main>`: the text goes from English straight to Ukrainian.

## What can go wrong

### 1. Every app calls `i18next.init` → the last one wins
- **Scenario:** each app imports the default `i18next` (an MF singleton, so the same object) and runs
  `i18next.use(initReactI18next).init({ lng: 'en', resources: { en: { catalog: … } } })` in its exposed module.
- **Symptom:** no error. When catalog's module loads, the page switches to English (`languageChanged -> en` fires) and
  the shell's texts turn into keys (`title` instead of `Маркетплейс`). Confirmed with a short script: after the second
  `init`, `i18n.language === 'en'` and `hasResourceBundle('uk', 'shell') === false`. Which app wins depends on which
  remote the user opened last.
- **Root cause:** `init` is not additive: it replaces the options, creates a new resource store from `resources` and
  sets `lng` again. Sharing the library as a singleton shares the instance, and with it whoever initializes last.
- **Fix:** (chosen) one owner. Only the shell's `bootstrap.tsx` creates and initializes an instance
  (`createInstance()`, so a stray `i18next.init()` on the default export cannot touch it) and passes it through
  `<I18nextProvider>`; remotes add namespaces, never options. Alternatives: separate instances per remote
  (`createInstance` in each exposed module) synchronized on `languageChanged` — every remote needs a subscription, and
  two instances can disagree; not sharing i18next at all — same, plus duplicated code.

### 2. A remote loads its locales from the host's origin → 404
- **Scenario A:** a remote uses `i18next-http-backend` (or `fetch`) with `loadPath: '/locales/{{lng}}/{{ns}}.json'`.
  A root-relative URL resolves against the **page**, which is `http://localhost:3000` when hosted.
- **Scenario B:** the remote's `output.publicPath` is `'/'` (or a fixed URL) instead of `'auto'`.
- **Symptom:** A — `GET http://localhost:3000/locales/uk/catalog.json 404 (Not Found)` (confirmed with `curl` on the
  shell dev server; `historyApiFallback` does not rewrite paths with a dot), keys rendered instead of texts. Works in
  standalone mode, where page origin and remote origin are the same — so it is found only after integration.
  B — every chunk of the remote, not only locales, is requested from the shell: `404` for
  `http://localhost:3000/src_exposed_App_tsx.js`, then
  `ChunkLoadError: Loading chunk … failed. (error: http://localhost:3000/vendors-…-fffe9c.js) while loading "./App"
  from webpack/container/reference/catalog`, blank page (confirmed by temporarily setting `publicPath: '/'`; reverted).
  If a file with the same name exists on the host (`locale-uk.js` exists in both apps), the request even succeeds but
  pushes into the host's chunk registry, so the remote's chunk never resolves.
- **Root cause:** URLs are resolved against the document, not against the code that issues them. Only webpack's
  runtime knows where the remote was loaded from, via `publicPath: 'auto'`.
- **Fix:** (chosen) load translations as webpack chunks of the remote (`import('./locales/en.json')`): the URL is built
  from the remote's `__webpack_require__.p`, and the file is part of the remote's build output. Alternatives:
  resolve URLs explicitly against the public path — `new URL('locales/en.json', __webpack_public_path__)` or
  `new URL('./locales/en.json', import.meta.url)` (an asset module, also hashed by webpack); runtime config with each
  remote's base URL (iteration 09/13); a CDN path known to everyone.

## Trade-offs and alternatives
| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| Loader backend, remote-registered loaders (chosen) | i18next's own load-then-switch; lazy; remote owns texts and loading; shell knows nothing | Small cross-bundle API found by shape on `instance.modules.backend`; switch also reloads namespaces of apps visited earlier |
| Remote calls `addResourceBundle`, Suspense waits | No backend at all | react-i18next 17 uses `useSyncExternalStore`, so `startTransition` cannot hold the old UI: Suspense fallback flashes on every switch (confirmed) |
| Shell backend → remote `./i18n` expose | No registration API | Shell lists every remote's namespace; one more expose to keep in sync per remote |
| `i18next-http-backend` with `loadPath` per namespace | Standard plugin, translators can update files without a rebuild | Shell knows remote origins and file layout; no webpack hashing; new dependency |
| Eager bundles | Simplest, no loading states | Every language of every app downloaded up front; shell redeploy for a text change if bundled there |
| Each remote its own instance | Full isolation | Language must be synchronized by hand; two sources of truth |

## Interview questions
- **Q:** Who owns translations in a micro-frontend architecture?
  **A:** The team that owns the UI. Texts ship with the remote (one namespace per app), so a text change is a remote
  deploy. The host owns only the instance and the current language — like it owns the router and the QueryClient.
- **Q:** Why must i18next and react-i18next be shared singletons?
  **A:** react-i18next keeps the instance in a React context; a second copy of the library is a second context, so a
  remote would not see the shell's provider. One copy of i18next means one language and one resource store.
- **Q:** Why does `publicPath` matter for remote assets?
  **A:** Every chunk, CSS file and asset URL of a remote is built from its runtime's public path. `'auto'` computes it
  from the URL of `remoteEntry.js`, so the remote loads its own files from its own origin wherever it is hosted. A
  root-relative URL or `publicPath: '/'` points at the host and fails only after integration.
- **Q:** How do you switch the language in all micro-frontends without a flash of untranslated text?
  **A:** Let i18next load the new language of every used namespace first and only then emit `languageChanged`
  (`changeLanguage` does this when the namespaces go through a backend). A React transition does not help when the
  library updates through `useSyncExternalStore`.
- **Q:** Why format numbers and dates with `Intl` and not by hand?
  **A:** Locale rules (decimal separators, currency placement, month names, plural categories — Ukrainian has four)
  are built into the platform; i18next's formatters (`currency`, `datetime`, plurals) are thin wrappers over
  `Intl.NumberFormat`, `Intl.DateTimeFormat` and `Intl.PluralRules`.
- **Q:** What happens if two remotes use the same namespace?
  **A:** The second registration replaces the first loader and both write into one resource bundle — keys collide.
  Namespace names are a cross-app contract: one per app, named after the container.
